nodes.title: Calc 3 Tutor
nodes.body: Answer a few questions and I'll walk you to the exact setup. You do the arithmetic.

nodes.title: What do you see?
nodes.body: Pick what best matches the problem statement.

choices.label: An integral is already written with bounds
A region or solid: find area, volume, mass, centroid, average
A surface: find its surface area
A curve/path: ∫ f ds, work, wire mass, ∫F·dr
A closed curve in the plane (∮)
Is F conservative? Find a potential f

nodes.title: Choosing a method
nodes.body:
Rectangle in 2D → Cartesian ∬
Curves/lines bound region → Type I / II
Inner antiderivative impossible (e^(x²), sin(y²)) → reverse order
Circle, disk, ring, x²+y² → polar
Surface z=f(x,y), 'area of the part of' → surface area
Box, planes, tetrahedron → Cartesian ∭
Cylinder/paraboloid around z-axis → cylindrical
Sphere, ball, cone + sphere, x²+y²+z² → spherical
Wire density, ds, arc length → scalar line ∫
Force, work, F·dr, P dx + Q dy → vector line ∫
Endpoints only matter / P_y = Q_x → potential function
Closed plane curve → Green
Spreading out → div;  spinning → curl

nodes.title: Look at the bounds
nodes.body: Are all four bounds numbers (constants)?

choices.label: No, inner bounds have x or y

nodes.title: Can you do the inner integral?
nodes.body: Try the inner antiderivative in your head. Red flags: e^(x²), e^(y²), sin(x²), cos(y³), √(1+x³), e^(x/y) integrated in the wrong variable.

choices.label: Integrand has x²+y² and bounds look circular

nodes.title: Read bounds → region
nodes.body:
1. Turn bounds into inequalities. Outer bounds are numbers; inner bounds are curves.
Ex: ∫0→1 ∫(x²)→(√x) dy dx  ⇒  0≤x≤1, x²≤y≤√x.
2. Draw the inner curves (y=x², y=√x) and the outer lines (x=0, x=1).
3. Shade between the inner curves, only for x in the outer range.
4. Test a point: pick x in the middle, check lower curve < upper curve there.
nodes.warn: Outer bounds are always constants. If inner bounds depend on x, the outer variable is x.

nodes.title: Read bounds → solid
nodes.body:
1. Write all 6 inequalities, innermost first.
2. Innermost pair = bottom & top surfaces (e.g. z from 0 to 4−x²−y² ⇒ under a paraboloid, above z=0).
3. Outer two pairs = the shadow region in the plane of the other two variables. Sketch it.
4. Stack: shadow on the floor, surfaces as floor and ceiling.
Recognize: x²+y² terms → round (paraboloid, cone, cylinder); linear → planes; √(a²−x²−y²) → sphere.

nodes.title: Rectangle ∬
nodes.body:
R = [a,b]×[c,d]. Either order works (Fubini).
Area = ∬1 dA; volume under z=f≥0 = ∬f dA; average = (1/Area)∬f dA.
Pick the order that makes the inner integral easy.

nodes.title: Product shortcut
nodes.body:
Constant bounds and f = g(x)h(y) ⇒ multiply two single integrals.
Ex: ∬ x·e^y over [0,2]×[0,1] = (∫0→2 x dx)(∫0→1 e^y dy) = 2(e−1).
nodes.formula: ∫a→b∫c→d g(x)h(y) dy dx = (∫a→b g dx)(∫c→d h dy)

nodes.title: Choose the order
nodes.body:
If the integrand is x·e^(xy): integrate dy FIRST. The x outside is exactly the chain-rule factor:
∫ x·e^(xy) dy = e^(xy).
Same for x·cos(xy) → sin(xy). For y·e^(xy) or y·cos(xy), do dx first, since d/dx(xy) = y.
Rule: inner variable = the one whose coefficient sits outside the composite.

nodes.title: Evaluate iterated ∫
nodes.body:
1. Inner integral: integrate in the inner variable only. Every other letter is a constant.
2. Plug in inner bounds: (upper) − (lower). Bounds may be functions; substitute them fully.
3. Simplify to a single-variable expression.
4. Outer integral, plug bounds, subtract.
Need an antiderivative trick? See the Integration toolkit.
nodes.warn: Don't drop a term when plugging in bounds. Write (upper) − (lower) with parentheses.

nodes.title: Volume between surfaces
nodes.body:
Volume = ∬D (top − bottom) dA.
1. Identify top surface and bottom surface (bottom may be z=0).
2. D = shadow on xy-plane. Edge of shadow: where top = bottom, or given walls.
3. Choose coordinates for D.
nodes.warn: Check which surface is on top by testing a point inside D.

nodes.title: Area
nodes.body: Integrand = 1.

nodes.title: Volume
nodes.body: Integrand = f(x,y) (height). If between two surfaces, use top − bottom.

nodes.title: Mass
nodes.body: Integrand = density δ(x,y).

nodes.title: Average value
nodes.body: Compute ∬f dA and the area of D, then divide.

choices.label: Disk, sector, ring, centered at origin

nodes.title: General region
nodes.body:
1. Sketch every boundary curve.
2. Find intersection points: set the curves equal and solve.
3. Draw a vertical line through D: does it always enter through the same curve and leave through the same curve? Then Type I works.
4. Draw a horizontal line: same test for Type II.

choices.label: Vertical line test passes (Type I, dy dx)
Horizontal line test passes (Type II, dx dy)

nodes.title: Type I: dy dx
nodes.body:
x runs from leftmost to rightmost point of D (numbers, often intersection x-values).
y runs from bottom curve to top curve, both written as y = (in x).
Check: at a middle x, bottom value < top value.

nodes.title: Type II: dx dy
nodes.body:
y runs from lowest to highest point of D (numbers).
Solve each boundary for x. x runs from left curve to right curve.
Square roots: x = +√y on the right half, −√y on the left.

nodes.title: Split the region
nodes.body:
Find where the entering (or exiting) curve changes; that's at a corner/intersection.
Draw a line there to cut D into pieces that each pass the test.
Set up each piece separately and ADD the integrals.
Often the other order avoids splitting, so try it first.

nodes.title: Triangle region
nodes.body:
1. Plot the 3 vertices.
2. Line through (x1,y1),(x2,y2): slope m = (y2−y1)/(x2−x1), then y = y1 + m(x − x1). Solve for x instead if doing dx first.
3. Pick the order where one side is the bottom (or left) and one side is the top (or right). Otherwise split at the middle vertex.
Area check: ½·base·height.
nodes.warn: Area of a triangle is ½bh, not bh.

nodes.title: Reverse the order
nodes.body:
1. Write bounds as inequalities.
2. Sketch: inner curves + outer lines; shade.
3. Label every corner (solve intersections).
4. New OUTER variable: its min and max over the whole region (numbers).
5. Solve each boundary curve for the new INNER variable (x = arcsin y ⇔ y = sin x; x = ln y ⇔ y = eˣ; y = x² ⇔ x = √y).
6. Draw a line in the new direction: inner bound = curve you enter → curve you exit.
7. If the entering/exiting curve changes, split.
nodes.warn: Never just swap dx and dy. The region stays the same; the bounds change.

nodes.title: Example
nodes.body:
∫0→1 ∫y→1 e^(x²) dx dy  (can't integrate e^(x²) dx)
Region: 0≤y≤1, y≤x≤1. Triangle with corners (0,0),(1,0),(1,1).
New outer: x from 0 to 1. Vertical line at x: y from 0 up to y = x.
= ∫0→1 ∫0→x e^(x²) dy dx = ∫0→1 x·e^(x²) dx
u = x²: = ½(e − 1).
Notice the new inner integral created the factor x that u-sub needs.

nodes.title: Polar: describe D
nodes.body: x = r cosθ, y = r sinθ, x²+y² = r², dA = r dr dθ.

choices.label: Part of a disk (half, quadrant, wedge)
Bounded by a line like y=c or x=c
Inside a polar curve r = g(θ)

nodes.title: Full disk
nodes.body: x²+y² ≤ R² ⇒ r goes to R (not R²).

nodes.title: Angle bounds
nodes.body:
Quadrant I: 0→π/2   II: π/2→π
Upper half (y≥0): 0→π
Right half (x≥0): −π/2→π/2
Left half: π/2→3π/2   Lower: π→2π
Line y = x (QI): θ = π/4
y = √3·x: θ = π/3;  y = x/√3: θ = π/6
y-axis: θ = π/2. General line y = mx: θ = arctan(m).
Go counterclockwise: smaller angle is lower bound.

nodes.title: Annulus
nodes.body: Inner circle radius R1, outer circle radius R2.
nodes.formula: R1 ≤ r ≤ R2,  θ as needed

nodes.title: Circle through origin
nodes.body:
Substitute r² for x²+y², r sinθ for y, r cosθ for x, cancel one r.
x²+y² = 2ay ⇒ r = 2a sinθ, θ from 0 to π (circle above x-axis).
x²+y² = 2ax ⇒ r = 2a cosθ, θ from −π/2 to π/2.
r goes from 0 to that curve.
nodes.warn: If the problem gives (x−a)²+y² = a², expand it first: x²+y² = 2ax.

nodes.title: Line boundary
nodes.body:
y = c ⇒ r sinθ = c ⇒ r = c/sinθ = c·cscθ.
x = c ⇒ r = c·secθ.
Ex: inside x²+y²=4, above y=1: r from cscθ to 2.
θ where they meet: 2 sinθ = 1 ⇒ θ = π/6 to 5π/6.

nodes.title: Cartesian → polar
nodes.body:
1. Read the bounds as a region (sketch).
Clues: y from 0 to √(R²−x²) ⇒ upper half disk radius R.
x from −√(R²−y²) to √(R²−y²) ⇒ full width of a disk.
y from x to √(2−x²) ⇒ wedge between line y=x and circle r=√2.
y from 0 to √(2ax − x²), x from 0 to 2a ⇒ upper half of x²+y² = 2ax ⇒ r ≤ 2a cosθ, 0 ≤ θ ≤ π/2.
2. Write polar bounds for that region.

nodes.title: Convert & integrate
nodes.body:
1. Replace x = r cosθ, y = r sinθ, x²+y² = r².
2. Multiply by the Jacobian r.
3. Usually integrate dr first, then dθ.
4. If integrand = g(r)h(θ) and bounds are constants, split into a product.
Ex: ∬(x²+y²) dA → ∫∫ r²·r dr dθ = ∫∫ r³ dr dθ.
Ex: e^(−(x²+y²)) → e^(−r²)·r, u = r².
nodes.formula: ∬D f dA = ∫α→β ∫ r1→r2 f(r cosθ, r sinθ) r dr dθ
nodes.warn: Forgetting the extra r is the #1 polar mistake. Use radians.

nodes.title: Surface area, z = f(x,y)
nodes.body:
1. Compute f_x and f_y.
2. Integrand √(1 + f_x² + f_y²).
3. D = shadow in the xy-plane: 'part of z=f above region D' or 'below z=h' ⇒ f(x,y) ≤ h.
4. Choose coordinates for D.
nodes.warn: Don't forget the 1 inside the root. You integrate the stretch factor, not f.

choices.label: Radicand has x²+y² / D is a disk

nodes.title: Use polar
nodes.warn: Still need the polar r. It's what makes the u-sub work.

nodes.title: Constant factor
nodes.body:
If √(1+f_x²+f_y²) = k is constant, A = k · Area(D).
Ex: z = 2x+3y ⇒ k = √(1+4+9) = √14.

nodes.title: One-variable radicand
nodes.body:
Ex: z = y² ⇒ √(1+4y²); z = x^(3/2) ⇒ √(1 + 9x/4).
Integrate the OTHER variable first (it's just length of D in that direction), so the inner gives a factor that helps the u-sub.
If D is a triangle with y-dependent bounds, choose the order so the outer variable matches the radicand.

nodes.title: Part of a plane
nodes.body: Solve for z, or use the shortcut. D is the shadow on the xy-plane (e.g. first octant ⇒ triangle cut by z=0: ax+by=d).

nodes.title: Part of a sphere
nodes.body:
z = √(a²−x²−y²) ⇒ √(1+f_x²+f_y²) = a/√(a²−r²).
A = ∫∫ a/√(a²−r²) · r dr dθ. u = a² − r².
Shadow D: where the sphere meets the other surface (set equal, solve for r).

nodes.title: Parametric surface
nodes.body: Compute r_u, r_v, their cross product, and its length.

nodes.title: What does the solid look like?

choices.label: Cylinder, paraboloid, cone with flat top, x²+y²
Paraboloid around x- or y-axis (x = y²+z²)

nodes.title: Which coordinates?
nodes.body:
Look at the surfaces after converting:
Only planes → Cartesian.
x²+y² appears, round shadow, z-axis symmetry → cylindrical (dV = r dz dr dθ).
x²+y²+z² appears, or cone + sphere → spherical (dV = ρ² sinφ dρ dφ dθ).
Cone + plane z = h: either works; cylindrical is usually simpler.

nodes.title: Triple ∫ setup
nodes.body:
1. List all bounding surfaces.
2. Innermost variable = the one with a clear floor & ceiling (usually z).
3. Write z from bottom(x,y) to top(x,y).
4. Shadow D on xy-plane: set top = bottom to find its edge, plus any walls.
5. Describe D like a 2D region (Type I/II).
nodes.formula: ∭E f dV = ∬D ∫ bottom→top f dz dA
nodes.warn: A bound may use only OUTER variables, never one already integrated.

nodes.title: Tetrahedron
nodes.body:
Plane x/a + y/b + z/c = 1 in the first octant.
z: 0 → c(1 − x/a − y/b)
Shadow (set z=0): line x/a + y/b = 1.
y: 0 → b(1 − x/a);  x: 0 → a.
Plane given as 2x+3y+z=6? Intercepts: x=3, y=2, z=6.
Volume check: abc/6.

nodes.title: Evaluate ∭
nodes.body:
Inside out: innermost variable first, treat others as constants, plug bounds.
After the first integration you have a double integral; after the second, a single.
For volume, the inner dz integral gives (top − bottom).

nodes.title: Change order (3D)
nodes.body:
1. Write all 6 inequalities. Sketch the solid.
2. Pick the new innermost variable; solve every surface for it.
3. Inner bounds: the two surfaces it runs between.
4. Project onto the plane of the remaining 2 variables: eliminate the inner variable (set the two surfaces equal, or set it to its extreme like 0).
5. Describe that 2D shadow in the new order.
6. Split if a boundary changes partway.

nodes.title: Example
nodes.body:
∫0→1 ∫0→(1−x) ∫0→(1−x−y) f dz dy dx  (tetrahedron x+y+z ≤ 1)
Want dx dz dy:
x: 0 → 1−y−z (solve plane for x)
Shadow on yz-plane (x=0): y+z ≤ 1 ⇒ z: 0 → 1−y
y: 0 → 1
⇒ ∫0→1 ∫0→(1−y) ∫0→(1−y−z) f dx dz dy
Curved example: z ≤ 1−y², x from 0 to 2: shadow in yz-plane is under the parabola.

nodes.title: Cylindrical setup
nodes.body:
Convert each surface:
x²+y² = R² → r = R (cylinder)
z = √(x²+y²) → z = r (cone); z = k√(x²+y²) → z = kr
z = x²+y² → z = r² (paraboloid)
z = a − x²−y² → z = a − r²
sphere → z = ±√(R² − r²)
plane z = y → z = r sinθ

choices.label: Round around x- or y-axis (x = y²+z²)

nodes.title: Cylindrical bounds
nodes.body:
z: bottom surface → top surface (in r, θ).
r: 0 → edge of shadow. Edge = where top = bottom (solve for r) or the cylinder wall.
θ: 0 → 2π unless cut (first octant 0→π/2; y≥0: 0→π; x≥0: −π/2→π/2).
Off-center cylinder x²+y² = 2ax ⇒ r ≤ 2a cosθ, −π/2 ≤ θ ≤ π/2.
nodes.formula: ∫θ ∫r ∫ z_bot→z_top f · r dz dr dθ
nodes.warn: Cone z=r vs paraboloid z=r²: they meet at r = 1. Which is on top for 0<r<1? r > r², so the cone.

nodes.title: Examples
nodes.body:
Between z = x²+y² and z = 4:
V = ∫0→2π ∫0→2 (4 − r²) r dr dθ = 2π(8 − 4) = 8π.

Inside sphere x²+y²+z² = 2, above cone z = r:
z: r → √(2 − r²); meet: r = √(2−r²) ⇒ r = 1.
V = ∫0→2π ∫0→1 (√(2−r²) − r) r dr dθ.

nodes.title: Cartesian → cylindrical
nodes.body:
1. Outer two bounds (x, y) describe the shadow: convert it to r, θ like polar.
2. z bounds: replace x²+y² with r².
3. Integrand: x = r cosθ, y = r sinθ, x²+y² = r².
4. Multiply by r.

nodes.title: Spherical: the solid
nodes.body: ρ = distance from origin. φ = angle down from +z axis (0 to π). θ = angle around z-axis.

choices.label: Ice-cream: above a cone, inside a sphere
Cut by a plane z = h

nodes.title: Ball pieces
nodes.body:
Full ball radius R: ρ 0→R, φ 0→π, θ 0→2π.
Upper hemisphere (z ≥ 0): φ 0→π/2.
Lower: φ π/2→π.
First octant: φ 0→π/2 and θ 0→π/2.
y ≥ 0 half: θ 0→π.

nodes.title: Converting surfaces
nodes.body:
x²+y²+z² = R² → ρ = R
z = √(x²+y²) → φ = π/4
z = √3·√(x²+y²) → φ = π/6
z = √((x²+y²)/3) → φ = π/3
General cone z = k√(x²+y²) → tanφ = 1/k
z = h (plane) → ρ = h secφ
x²+y² = a² (cylinder) → ρ = a cscφ
xy-plane → φ = π/2

nodes.title: Above cone, inside sphere
nodes.body:
Inside the cone (the part near the +z axis) ⇒ φ from 0 to the cone's angle φ0.
Cone z = √(x²+y²): φ0 = π/4.
Sphere centered at origin radius R: ρ 0→R.
θ 0→2π.
nodes.warn: Outside/below the cone (but above xy-plane) is φ0 → π/2, not 0 → φ0.

nodes.title: Shifted sphere
nodes.body:
x²+y²+z² = 2az ⇒ ρ² = 2aρ cosφ ⇒ ρ = 2a cosφ.
(Sphere radius a, center (0,0,a), touches origin.)
ρ: 0 → 2a cosφ. Whole thing: φ 0→π/2.
Inside sphere AND above cone z = √(x²+y²): φ 0→π/4.
Inside sphere but OUTSIDE (below) that cone: φ π/4→π/2.
nodes.warn: The ρ bound depends on φ, so integrate ρ first.

nodes.title: Spherical shell
nodes.body: Then the φ, θ bounds of whatever piece is described.

nodes.title: Plane z = h
nodes.body:
z = h ⇒ ρ cosφ = h ⇒ ρ = h secφ.
Cone capped by plane (below z=h, above cone): ρ 0 → h secφ, φ 0 → φ0.
Cap of sphere above z=h: ρ h secφ → R, φ 0 → arccos(h/R).
(arccos from where plane meets sphere: R cosφ = h.)

nodes.title: Cartesian → spherical
nodes.body:
1. Identify the solid from the bounds:
z from √(x²+y²) to √(R²−x²−y²) ⇒ ice-cream cone.
z from 0 to √(R²−x²−y²) ⇒ upper half ball.
2. Write spherical bounds.
3. Convert integrand and multiply by ρ² sinφ.

nodes.title: Integrand & Jacobian
nodes.body:
x = ρ sinφ cosθ
y = ρ sinφ sinθ
z = ρ cosφ
x²+y²+z² = ρ²;  √(x²+y²) = ρ sinφ
Order dρ dφ dθ. If all bounds are constants, it splits into 3 single integrals.
nodes.formula: dV = ρ² sinφ dρ dφ dθ
nodes.warn: Don't forget ρ² sinφ. Don't swap φ (from z-axis) and θ (around).

nodes.title: Evaluate
nodes.body:
ρ integral: ∫ρ² dρ = ρ³/3, ∫ρ³ dρ = ρ⁴/4.
If ρ bound is 2a cosφ: get (2a cosφ)³/3 · sinφ ⇒ u = cosφ.
∫ cosⁿφ sinφ dφ = −cosⁿ⁺¹φ/(n+1).
∫0→π sinφ dφ = 2;  ∫0→π/2 sinφ dφ = 1;
∫0→π/4 sinφ dφ = 1 − √2/2.
∫0→2π dθ = 2π.
e^(x²+y²+z²) = e^(ρ²): with ρ² from dV, ∫ρ³e^(ρ²) dρ: u = ρ², then by parts.

nodes.title: Lamina centroid
nodes.body:
1. m = ∬ δ dA (uniform δ: use Area).
2. M_y = ∬ x δ dA,  M_x = ∬ y δ dA.
3. Same bounds for all three integrals.
Symmetry: D symmetric across y-axis (and δ too) ⇒ x̄ = 0.
nodes.formula: x̄ = M_y / m,   ȳ = M_x / m
nodes.warn: M_y uses x (moment about the y-axis). Easy to swap.

nodes.title: Solid centroid
nodes.body:
1. Symmetry: round around z-axis ⇒ x̄ = ȳ = 0. Only find z̄.
2. m = ∭ δ dV (uniform: use volume V).
3. M_xy = ∭ z δ dV. In spherical z = ρ cosφ ⇒ integrand ρ³ sinφ cosφ. In cylindrical z·r.
4. z̄ = M_xy / m.
nodes.warn: z̄ can't be 0 if the solid is entirely above the xy-plane. z̄ must be between the lowest and highest z of the solid.

choices.label: Example: cone below sphere at origin

nodes.title: Cone in shifted sphere
nodes.body:
Above z = √(x²+y²), inside x²+y²+z² = 2z.
ρ: 0→2cosφ, φ: 0→π/4, θ: 0→2π.
V = 2π ∫0→π/4 (8cos³φ/3) sinφ dφ
  = 2π·(8/3)·¼(1 − ¼) = π
M = 2π ∫0→π/4 (16cos⁴φ/4) cosφ sinφ dφ
  = 2π·4·(1/6)(1 − 1/8) = 7π/6
z̄ = 7/6, x̄ = ȳ = 0. (Solid spans z 0→2 ✓)

nodes.title: What's being integrated?
nodes.body: Keywords decide it.

choices.label: Scalar: ∫ f ds, arc length, wire density/mass
Vector: work, force, ∫ F·dr, ∫ P dx + Q dy
∫ f dx  or  ∫ f dy alone

nodes.title: Parameterize the path
nodes.body:
Segment A → B: r(t) = A + t(B − A), 0 ≤ t ≤ 1.
Circle radius a, CCW: (a cos t, a sin t), 0→2π. Quarter in QI: 0→π/2.
Clockwise: (a cos t, −a sin t), or run t backward.
Ellipse: (a cos t, b sin t).
Graph y = g(x), x: a→b: (t, g(t)), t: a→b.
Graph x = g(y) (e.g. x = y²+4): (g(t), t), t from start y to end y.
Polygon / piecewise path: do each piece, then add.
nodes.warn: Direction matters for work: start point at the lower t.

nodes.title: Scalar line ∫ f ds
nodes.body:
1. Parameterize r(t), a ≤ t ≤ b.
2. r'(t).
3. Speed |r'(t)| = √(x'² + y'² + z'²).
4. Plug r(t) into f.
5. ∫ f(r(t))·|r'(t)| dt.
Mass of wire = ∫ δ ds. Length = ∫ 1 ds.
nodes.warn: ds ≠ dt. Include the speed. Don't forget the density.

nodes.title: Parameterize the path
nodes.body:
Segment A → B: r(t) = A + t(B − A), 0 ≤ t ≤ 1.
Circle radius a, CCW: (a cos t, a sin t), 0→2π. Quarter in QI: 0→π/2.
Clockwise: (a cos t, −a sin t), or run t backward.
Ellipse: (a cos t, b sin t).
Graph y = g(x), x: a→b: (t, g(t)), t: a→b.
Graph x = g(y) (e.g. x = y²+4): (g(t), t), t from start y to end y.
Polygon / piecewise path: do each piece, then add.
nodes.warn: Direction matters for work: start point at the lower t.

nodes.title: Example
nodes.body:
∫C (x + y) ds, segment (0,0)→(3,4).
r = (3t, 4t), r' = (3,4), speed = 5.
f = 3t + 4t = 7t.
∫0→1 7t·5 dt = 35/2.
Circle radius a: speed = a. Segment: speed = |B − A|.

nodes.title: Work ∫ F·dr
nodes.body: Before grinding, look for shortcuts.

nodes.title: Direct computation
nodes.body:
1. Parameterize r(t) (start → end).
2. r'(t).
3. F(r(t)): plug x(t), y(t), z(t) into F.
4. Dot product F(r(t))·r'(t). It's a scalar.
5. Integrate in t.
P dx + Q dy form: dx = x'(t) dt, dy = y'(t) dt.
nodes.warn: Dot product, not magnitude. Reversing the path flips the sign.

nodes.title: Parameterize the path
nodes.body:
Segment A → B: r(t) = A + t(B − A), 0 ≤ t ≤ 1.
Circle radius a, CCW: (a cos t, a sin t), 0→2π. Quarter in QI: 0→π/2.
Clockwise: (a cos t, −a sin t), or run t backward.
Ellipse: (a cos t, b sin t).
Graph y = g(x), x: a→b: (t, g(t)), t: a→b.
Graph x = g(y) (e.g. x = y²+4): (g(t), t), t from start y to end y.
Polygon / piecewise path: do each piece, then add.
nodes.warn: Direction matters for work: start point at the lower t.

nodes.title: ∫ f dx or ∫ f dy
nodes.body:
Parameterize, then dx = x'(t) dt (or dy = y'(t) dt). No speed factor.
Shortcut: ∫ g(x) dx alone depends only on the x-endpoints: = G(x_end) − G(x_start).

nodes.title: Parameterize the path
nodes.body:
Segment A → B: r(t) = A + t(B − A), 0 ≤ t ≤ 1.
Circle radius a, CCW: (a cos t, a sin t), 0→2π. Quarter in QI: 0→π/2.
Clockwise: (a cos t, −a sin t), or run t backward.
Ellipse: (a cos t, b sin t).
Graph y = g(x), x: a→b: (t, g(t)), t: a→b.
Graph x = g(y) (e.g. x = y²+4): (g(t), t), t from start y to end y.
Polygon / piecewise path: do each piece, then add.
nodes.warn: Direction matters for work: start point at the lower t.

nodes.title: 2D test
nodes.body:
Compute P_y and Q_x.
Equal (on all of ℝ² or a simply connected domain) ⇒ conservative.
Not equal ⇒ not conservative; line integrals depend on path.
nodes.warn: Watch domains with holes (e.g. F undefined at origin): equal partials there don't guarantee conservative.

nodes.title: 3D test
nodes.body:
Check all three: P_y = Q_x, P_z = R_x, Q_z = R_y.
(That's curl F = 0.)

nodes.title: Find f (2D)
nodes.body:
1. f = ∫ P dx + g(y).
2. Differentiate: f_y = (stuff) + g'(y).
3. Set f_y = Q. Solve for g'(y). It must have only y.
4. Integrate g'. f is a SCALAR.
Ex: F = ⟨2xy + 1, x² + 3y²⟩
f = x²y + x + g(y); f_y = x² + g' = x² + 3y² ⇒ g = y³.
f = x²y + x + y³. Check: ∇f = F.
nodes.warn: Don't forget g(y). Integrating P alone misses pure-y terms.

nodes.title: Find f (3D)
nodes.body:
1. f = ∫ P dx + g(y,z).
2. f_y = Q ⇒ find g_y, integrate in y: g = … + h(z).
3. f_z = R ⇒ find h'(z), integrate.
Ex: F = ⟨y, x + z, y⟩: f = xy + g(y,z); f_y = x + g_y = x + z ⇒ g = yz + h(z); f_z = y + h' = y ⇒ h = 0. f = xy + yz.

nodes.title: Fundamental theorem
nodes.body:
Work = potential at the end minus potential at the start. Path doesn't matter.
Closed curve ⇒ 0.

nodes.title: Green's theorem?
nodes.body: Green needs: closed, simple, plane curve, and P, Q smooth on the whole inside.

choices.label: Asked to verify: do it both ways

nodes.title: Clockwise
nodes.body: Positive orientation = CCW (region on your left). For clockwise, compute with Green and NEGATE.

nodes.title: Open path
nodes.body: Green doesn't apply directly. Options: compute directly, check if conservative, or close the path with a segment, use Green, then subtract the added segment's integral.

nodes.title: Apply Green
nodes.body:
1. P = coefficient of dx, Q = coefficient of dy.
2. Compute Q_x and P_y.
3. Integrand Q_x − P_y.
4. D = region inside C. Set up ∬D.
nodes.formula: ∮C P dx + Q dy = ∬D (Q_x − P_y) dA
nodes.warn: It's Q_x − P_y (Q first). Reversing it flips the sign.

choices.label: Q_x − P_y is a constant k

nodes.title: Constant integrand
nodes.body:
∮ = k · Area(D).
Triangle ½bh, disk πR², ellipse πab, rectangle lw.
nodes.warn: Use the actual region's area (triangle ≠ rectangle).

nodes.title: Direct and Green
nodes.body:
Green side: ∬D (Q_x − P_y) dA.
Direct side: for each edge, parameterize A + t(B−A) in the CCW order, compute ∫ (P x' + Q y') dt, sum all edges.
The two answers must match. That's your check.

nodes.title: Gradient
nodes.body:
Input: scalar f. Output: vector.
Points toward fastest increase of f.

nodes.title: Divergence
nodes.body:
Input: vector F = ⟨P,Q,R⟩. Output: scalar.
>0: net outflow (source). <0: inflow (sink). =0: incompressible.
nodes.warn: Each component is differentiated by its OWN variable only.

nodes.title: Curl
nodes.body:
Input: vector. Output: vector.
Cyclic pattern x→y→z→x:
i: R_y − Q_z
j: P_z − R_x
k: Q_x − P_y
(Determinant with rows i j k / ∂x ∂y ∂z / P Q R; the j term gets a minus.)
curl F = 0 ⇒ irrotational. 2D field: curl = (Q_x − P_y) k.
nodes.warn: Order matters in each component. Check the j component's sign.

nodes.title: Laplacian
nodes.body:
Input: scalar f. Output: scalar. It's div(grad f).
Not always zero. (f with ∇²f = 0 is called harmonic.)

nodes.title: Meaningful?
nodes.body:
Work inside out, tracking scalar (S) or vector (V).
grad: S→V   div: V→S   curl: V→V   ∇²: S→S
OK: div(grad f), curl(grad f), grad(div F), div(curl F), curl(curl F)
Meaningless: curl(div F) [curl of scalar], div(div F), grad(grad f), grad F (F vector), div f (f scalar).

nodes.title: Identities
nodes.body: (For f, F with continuous 2nd partials.)
nodes.warn: curl of grad is the ZERO VECTOR; div of grad is the Laplacian (not 0 in general).

choices.label: Sign of the integral / is it zero?
Vector field picture: div or curl sign
Line integral sign from a picture
Pick the integral for a pictured region
Pick the figure: field arrows on a curve

nodes.title: Match integral to solid
nodes.body:
Check each candidate:
1. Right Jacobian? (r for cyl/polar, ρ² sinφ for spherical, none for Cartesian.)
2. Innermost bounds = floor/ceiling of the solid.
3. Outer bounds = the shadow; edge where surfaces meet.
4. Plug a test point to confirm top > bottom.
5. Volume integrand should be 1 (times Jacobian).

nodes.title: Sign / symmetry
nodes.body:
Integrand > 0 on all of D ⇒ integral > 0.
Odd symmetry ⇒ 0: if D is symmetric across the y-axis and f(−x,y) = −f(x,y), ∬ f = 0. E.g. ∬ x dA over a disk = 0; ∬ x y² over a disk = 0.
Same with y and the x-axis.
For a picture: compare how much region is in f>0 vs f<0.

nodes.title: Reading a field plot
nodes.body:
Divergence at a point: arrows point away / get longer as you move along the flow ⇒ positive. Arrows converge / shrink ⇒ negative.
Curl (k-component): drop a paddle wheel. Spins CCW ⇒ positive, CW ⇒ negative. Arrows longer on one side than the other also means rotation.
Uniform parallel arrows ⇒ div = 0 and curl = 0.

nodes.title: Sign from a picture
nodes.body:
Walk along C in its direction.
F mostly WITH your motion ⇒ ∫F·dr > 0. Against ⇒ < 0. Perpendicular ⇒ ≈ 0.
Closed loop with nonzero circulation ⇒ F not conservative.
Scalar ∫ f ds ignores direction; sign comes from f only.

nodes.title: Coordinates
nodes.formula:
Polar: x=r cosθ, y=r sinθ
  dA = r dr dθ
Cyl: + z=z
  dV = r dz dr dθ
Sph: x=ρ sinφ cosθ
  y=ρ sinφ sinθ
  z=ρ cosφ
  dV = ρ² sinφ dρ dφ dθ
x²+y² = r² = ρ² sin²φ
x²+y²+z² = ρ²

nodes.title: Geometry
nodes.formula:
Area = ∬ 1 dA
V = ∭ 1 dV = ∬ (top−bot) dA
Surf = ∬ √(1+f_x²+f_y²) dA
m = ∭ δ dV
x̄ = ∭ xδ dV / m (same for ȳ, z̄)
2D: x̄ = M_y/m, M_y = ∬ xδ dA
avg f = ∬ f dA / Area

nodes.title: Line integrals
nodes.formula:
∫ f ds = ∫ f(r(t)) |r'(t)| dt
∫ F·dr = ∫ F(r(t))·r'(t) dt
Segment: r = A + t(B−A)
∫ ∇f·dr = f(B) − f(A)
2D conservative: P_y = Q_x
Green: ∮ P dx + Q dy
  = ∬ (Q_x − P_y) dA

nodes.title: Operators
nodes.formula:
∇f = ⟨f_x, f_y, f_z⟩
∇·F = P_x + Q_y + R_z
∇×F = ⟨R_y−Q_z, P_z−R_x, Q_x−P_y⟩
∇²f = f_xx + f_yy + f_zz
∇×∇f = 0,  ∇·(∇×F) = 0

nodes.title: u-substitution
nodes.body:
Look for a function and its derivative (up to a constant).
x·e^(x²): u = x², du = 2x dx ⇒ ½e^(x²)
r√(1+4r²): u = 1+4r² ⇒ (1/12)(1+4r²)^(3/2)
r·e^(−r²): ⇒ −½e^(−r²)
cosⁿφ sinφ: u = cosφ ⇒ −cosⁿ⁺¹φ/(n+1)
r/√(a²−r²): ⇒ −√(a²−r²)
Change the bounds too, or back-substitute.

nodes.title: Trig powers
nodes.body:
sin²θ = (1 − cos2θ)/2
cos²θ = (1 + cos2θ)/2
sinθ cosθ = ½ sin2θ
∫0→2π sin²θ dθ = ∫0→2π cos²θ dθ = π
∫0→π/2 sin²θ dθ = π/4
Odd power: save one factor, convert the rest with sin² = 1 − cos², then u-sub.

nodes.title: By parts
nodes.body:
∫u dv = uv − ∫v du.
Pick u by LIATE: Log, Inverse trig, Algebraic, Trig, Exponential.
∫ x e^x dx = (x − 1)e^x
∫ x cos x dx = x sin x + cos x
∫ ln x dx = x ln x − x

nodes.title: Standard values
nodes.body:
∫0→π sinφ dφ = 2
∫0→π/2 sinφ dφ = 1
∫0→π/2 cosθ dθ = 1
∫0→2π cosθ dθ = 0 = ∫0→2π sinθ dθ
∫0→π/2 sin³φ dφ = 2/3  (sin³ = (1 − cos²)·sin, u = cos)
∫ 1/(1+x²) = arctan x
∫ 1/√(1−x²) = arcsin x
cos(π/4) = sin(π/4) = √2/2
cos(π/6) = √3/2, sin(π/6) = ½
cos(π/3) = ½, sin(π/3) = √3/2

nodes.title: Before you box it
nodes.body:
☐ Jacobian: r (polar/cyl), ρ² sinφ (sph)
☐ Bounds: lower < upper; outer bounds are numbers
☐ Every term survived (upper) − (lower)
☐ Volume, area, mass, length > 0
☐ Orientation: CW or reversed path ⇒ flip sign
☐ Green: Q_x − P_y, not P_y − Q_x
☐ ds has the speed; dt doesn't
☐ Centroid lies inside the solid
☐ ½ for triangle area
☐ Radians, not degrees

nodes.title: Practice exam map
nodes.body: Find your question number, then follow the method.

choices.label: Q6–9 Type I / Type II regions
Q10 volume under plane over region
Q17 surface area of a plane
Q34 ∫ f dx along x = g(y)

nodes.title: Cross-section area
nodes.body:
Solid under z = f(x,y) over a rectangle.
Slice perpendicular to the x-axis at x = k: area A(k) = ∫ f(k, y) dy over the y-range.
Slice perpendicular to the y-axis at y = k: A(k) = ∫ f(x, k) dx over the x-range.
Volume = ∫ A(x) dx = ∫ A(y) dy (same answer both ways).
Ex: z = xy over [0,2]×[1,3]: A(x) = ∫1→3 xy dy = 4x; V = ∫0→2 4x dx = 8.
nodes.formula: A(x) = ∫c→d f(x,y) dy,   V = ∫a→b A(x) dx
nodes.warn: In A(x), x is a fixed number: only y is integrated.

nodes.title: Integral as a volume
nodes.body:
If f ≥ 0 and the solid is a known shape, use geometry.
z = √(R² − x²) ⇒ x² + z² = R², z ≥ 0: half of a circular cylinder of radius R lying along the y-axis.
Volume = (½πR²) × (length along y).
Ex: ∬ √(9 − y²) dA over [0,4]×[−3,3] = ½π(3²)·4 = 18π.
Need the x-range to cover the whole −R to R, else it's only part of the half-disk.

nodes.title: Area inside r = g(θ)
nodes.body:
r from 0 to the curve g(θ); θ over the sweep that traces the region once.
Inner integral ∫0→g r dr = ½g(θ)².
Read θ-limits from the picture: where does the curve start and end? (e.g. a spiral r = √θ starts at the origin at θ = 0.)
Ex: cardioid r = 1 + cosθ, θ 0→2π: A = ½∫(1+cosθ)² dθ = 3π/2.
nodes.formula: A = ∫α→β ∫0→g(θ) r dr dθ = ∫α→β ½ g(θ)² dθ

nodes.title: Round around x-axis
nodes.body:
x = a(y² + z²) is a paraboloid opening along the x-axis.
Use polar in the yz-plane: y = r cosθ, z = r sinθ, y²+z² = r².
x: from a r² up to the plane x = c.
Edge: a r² = c ⇒ r = √(c/a). θ: 0 → 2π.
dV = r dx dr dθ.
Ex: ∭ x dV, x = y²+z², x = 1:
∫0→2π ∫0→1 ∫r²→1 x·r dx dr dθ = π/3.
nodes.warn: Integrand x stays x (it's the axis variable). Only y, z become r, θ.

nodes.title: All six orders
nodes.body:
Solid: y = x², z = 0, y + 2z = 4.
Ranges: y 0→4, x ±√y, z 0→(4−y)/2.
dz dy dx: x −2→2, y x²→4, z 0→(4−y)/2
dz dx dy: y 0→4, x −√y→√y, z 0→(4−y)/2
dx dz dy: y 0→4, z 0→(4−y)/2, x −√y→√y
dx dy dz: z 0→2, y 0→4−2z, x −√y→√y
dy dz dx: x −2→2, z 0→(4−x²)/2, y x²→4−2z
dy dx dz: z 0→2, x ±√(4−2z), y x²→4−2z
Shadows: xy under y=4; yz triangle; xz under z=(4−x²)/2.
nodes.warn: Eliminate the inner variable to get the shadow: set y = x² into y + 2z = 4 ⇒ z = (4 − x²)/2.

nodes.title: Convert a point
nodes.body:
Cylindrical (r, θ, z):
x = r cosθ, y = r sinθ, z = z.
Ex: (2, π/3, 1) → (1, √3, 1).

Spherical, WebAssign/Stewart order (ρ, θ, φ):
x = ρ sinφ cosθ, y = ρ sinφ sinθ, z = ρ cosφ.
Ex: (4, π/2, π/3) → (0, 2√3, 2).

Back to cyl: r = √(x²+y²), tanθ = y/x (check quadrant).
Back to sph: ρ = √(x²+y²+z²), cosφ = z/ρ.
nodes.warn: Spherical points are written (ρ, θ, φ): θ is SECOND. φ = π/2 means z = 0.

nodes.title: Describe a solid
nodes.body:
θ range → which x, y signs:
0→π/2: x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0.  0→π: y ≥ 0, x any sign.
−π/2→π/2: x ≥ 0.
z sign: r ≤ z or 0 ≤ φ ≤ π/2 ⇒ z ≥ 0.
Top / bottom surfaces:
z = c plane;  z = r cone;  ρ = c sphere;  φ = c cone (c < π/2 opens up).
Slice in the xz-plane: set θ = 0 (and θ = π for x < 0). yz-plane: θ = π/2. Draw the 2D shape you get (triangle, sector, quarter-disk…).
nodes.warn: ρ ≤ c with φ ≤ φ0: top is part of a SPHERE, bottom part of a CONE.

nodes.title: Pick integral for a picture
nodes.body:
1. Round edges centered at origin ⇒ polar.
2. Read r: 0 to the radius. Read θ: from the start ray to the end ray, going counterclockwise (can start negative, e.g. −π/4 → 3π/4).
3. Correct answer must have f(r cosθ, r sinθ) AND the extra r.
Reject: f(r,θ) without conversion, missing r, or Cartesian bounds that don't match the picture.

nodes.title: Field arrows on a curve
nodes.body:
1. Curve shape: plot r(t) at t = 0, ½, 1 and compare. Ex (t³, t²): at t = ½ the point is (0.125, 0.25), so y > x early and the curve leaves the origin steeply.
2. For each listed t: point = r(t), arrow = F at that point.
3. Arrow direction: slope = F_y/F_x. Compare to the pictures.
4. Arrow length grows with |F|.
nodes.warn: The arrow is F at the point, not the tangent r'(t).

nodes.title: r = ⟨x,y,z⟩, r = |r|
nodes.body:
∇r = r/r   (unit radial vector)
∇×r = 0
∇·r = 3
∇(1/r) = −r/r³
∇(ln r) = r/r²
General: ∇(g(r)) = g'(r)·r/r
So ∇(rⁿ) = n rⁿ⁻² r.
nodes.warn: Bold r is the vector, plain r is its length. ∇ of a scalar gives a vector: answers must be vectors.
